About The Project#This project was created for one of my college courses about programming different systems that tie together a game engine. This is the final product of this course, but I wanted to continue development of the project at some point, since it was one of the classes I had the most fun developing in.
The Aero project combines a C++ base with a Lua scripting interface to provide fast development timelines. The current implmentation of the engine has the following features:
Currently written with mostly in C++ using Raylib as our base Small scale ECS GameObject system Custom scene file format Scripting capabilities using Lua Current State & Goals#The current implementation is very limited currently. There is no dedicated editor built to create scenes, there is only 2D capabilities, and limited physics integration. The project hopes to achieve these goals at the end of the development cycle:
No C++ scripting from end-user Lots of different utilities for development Luau language Integration A language created for the ROBLOX game engine, but has been open-sourced for a while. It adds a lot of nice features for development within the Lua stack and is generally more feature-rich than regular Lua. Built out editor Outside library integrations Jolt Physics Engine Either Vulkan Or DX12 Rendering Engine FMOD Sound Engine Better IDE integration for properly referencing and documenting each class object and method Repo Link#I would like to import my project files into the repository soon when life is less busy to me. I will keep updating this article with more information about the state of the project when those happen.
summary: A raylib based game engine that allows for Lua scripting.
title: Aero Engine

Role: Systems & UI Programmer#Choo Choo Boom Boom was made within the Game Studio @ Champlain College. This was the culmination of our efforts throughout the previous years at Champlain, and was made as our capstone project. I worked on some of the core gun systems including the sought after BFRG, as well as most of the core interface programming.
What is Choo Choo Boom Boom?#Choo Choo Boom Boom stems from the idea of a literal on-rails shooter. What if you were a train, with a gun, that fights an otherworldly entity?
Our team had conceptualized other ideas early on the development process for this game, such as one of the prototypes that I ended up working on, a game where you were a diver who would dive from ridiciously high heights. Choo Choo Boom Boom stood out as a project that had potential, and the team at In Scope Studio certainly wanted to prove it’s worth. Through rigorous development, the game made it throught the arduous greenlighting process, which kicked off the Spring production.
How can I play Choo Choo Boom Boom?#Steam Store Page
The game will be releasing on Steam on May 1st, and is participating in the annual Game Studio Senior Show!

Role: Gameplay, Systems, & UI Programmer#Timeline: Nov 2024 - Present#I started working on this project in the middle of development for the big Revamp update, which was a complete overhaul of the game with a very in-depth environment, fictionalized vehicles, and much more polished with more things to do compared to the old game. I am a core member of the programming team helping to creating this game, and I couldn’t be happier where I am.
Project Information#What is Southwest Florida?#Southwest Florida is a roleplaying game within the ROBLOX platform that aims to achieve a dense and smooth roleplaying environment. With more of a automotive focus, there are plenty of vehicles to drive, as well as a plethora of jobs to work and achieve income within the game’s economy.
What is the Revamp?#As described above, the revamp is a complete and utter overhaul of each portion of the game, including a brand new environment, programming, and plenty of new features to keep players busy. Before I started working on the revamp, it had already been in development for a couple years at the time, and the map was pretty much done.
This revamp allows us as developers to express full creative freedom within the limits of the engine, as well as adding features and certain things we think would be cool. It has allowed me also to create (in my opinion) some of the best work while working in a proper development environment. While we want to provide close-to-real vehicle handling, we still wanted to keep it driveable for players on all platforms. Roleplaying is the main focus, and we want to lean into that aspect a lot more.
What have you contributed?#Below are a few articles pertaining to major systems I have contributed towards. Keep in mind this list may change as the game gets closer to release. We aim to have this released by the end of Q2 2026.
Will update this page with specific things I worked on for this project when I can.

What can readers expect to see here?#Anything really! Depends on what I want to write or ramble about. It will most likely fall into these three categories:
Cool programming stuff or any new game development venture Garage project write-ups and videos Life achievements or updates I’ve really had a kick lately for wanting to record and document anything that I work on my garage, and will potentially be doing that in the next couple of months.
Documentation#For now, that section is a WIP. I need to consolidate libraries that I’ve released or want to release into this website, but first of all I need to get the rest of my portfolio projects into the website as well. What’s a portfolio website without any portfolio to view, right?
